incident-bot: PagerDuty alert PD-2025-INFER fired for service inference-prod (high token latency > 1200ms) — assigned to primary on-call Alex Chen
PagerDuty: https://pagerduty.example/incidents/PD-2025-INFER

Alex Chen: i'm seeing the spike on canary region. pulling logs now :eyes:
Alex Chen: starting tcpdump + tail on runtime logs
```bash
kubectl -n inference logs -l app=srv-inference -f --tail=200 | grep latency
# observed p95 ~ 1.8s, p99 ~ 2.4s
```

SupportBot: Alert correlated: increased queue depth on gpu-pool-3, autoscaler not launching new nodes (error: quota_exceeded)

Alex Chen: hmm autoscaler errors. I can try manual scale, but if PD expects ack in UI, i haven't clicked the PD ack (doing signal in slack instead)
PagerDuty: Escalation: primary did not acknowledge within 60s — paging secondary on-call Jordan Lee

Jordan Lee: on call, got the page. jumping in. handing off from Alex?
Alex Chen: handing to Jordan, i can keep digging if helpful but please take ownership. i didn't ack in PD because i was running commands, my bad.
PagerDuty: Incident PD-2025-INFER escalated to manager Samir Gupta due to escalation policy (timebox + severity). Manager notified.

Samir Gupta: on it — thanks. quick customer impact check: Maya, can you pull affected tenants?
Maya Torres: pulling from logs, sending list — looks like three enterprise tenants (acme-inc, bluehat, datawave) saw 500s and request timeouts between 17:52:10-17:54:22 UTC. Estimated impacted % of traffic: ~0.6% global.
Maya Torres: short summary for comms: intermittent 500s + elevated latency for text-generation endpoints; partial mitigation planned.

Jordan Lee: initial findings: kv-cache thrash after a failed tensor-quantize job caused memory pressure on gpu-pool-3 -> pods restarted -> latency spike. I'm scaling pool and will roll a probing config to redirect canary to pool-2.
Jordan Lee: running command to scale up nodes:
```bash
cloudctl scale-gpu-pool --name gpu-pool-3 --count 6
```
Jordan Lee: also bumping replica count for inference service to 8 to absorb backlog.

incident-bot: PagerDuty: PD-2025-INFER acknowledged by Jordan Lee at 1991234628

Alex Chen: thx. i'm going to patch the quantize job to avoid OOMs and redeploy.
Alex Chen: snippet of offending config:
```yaml
jobs:
  model-quantize:
    resources:
      limits:
        memory: 8Gi
```

Samir Gupta: decision: classify as Sev2 (partial customer impact, mitigation under way). Jordan, lead mitigation. Alex, follow up with root cause and postmortem. Maya, please prepare initial customer note for status page: short incident notice + impacted tenants + ETA for next update in 30m.
Maya Torres: drafting notice now — will post to status.redwood.ai after Sam approves.

Jordan Lee: scaling succeeded, new nodes added, pod restarts stopped. p95 latency back to ~220ms on canary. running 10m observation window.
Jordan Lee: will start controlled rollback of the latest runtime build to previous stable if metrics don't normalize in 10m.

SupportBot: Alert resolved on gpu-pool-3 autoscaler error (quota lambda cleared) — monitoring continues.

Samir Gupta: thanks everyone. since the manager page fired, i'll own external comms. Alex/Jordan pls add notes to the PD incident and mark who did what. we'll regroup for a 30-min postmortem once stable.

Jordan Lee: acknowledged. adding mitigation timeline to PD-2025-INFER.

incident-bot: PagerDuty: Incident PD-2025-INFER updated (status: acknowledged)

Maya Torres: posted initial status update: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/PD-2025-INFER — included affected tenants and next update ETA 30m

Alex Chen: quick note: i failed to click PD ack earlier while actively investigating — reminder for all: please ack in PD (not just slack) to prevent unnecessary escalations.
Samir Gupta: agreed. low-friction reminder: if you post "on it" in slack, please also ack PD. we'll add this to on-call runbook. :white_check_mark:

Jordan Lee: 10m observation window complete, metrics stable. I'll keep monitoring and then update PD to 'identified' with root cause hypothesis.

incident-bot: Thread closed for now — follow-ups tracked in PD-2025-INFER and the postmortem doc.
